title: Patriots Rule Out A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson for Dolphins Clash – ESPN Update
body:
New England’s roster will be missing two of its most dynamic offensive weapons for Sunday’s clash with the Miami Dolphins. Wide receiver A.J. Brown was placed on the injury list after a lingering knee problem flared up during practice, while second‑string running back TreVeyon Henderson was sidelined by an illness that forced him to stay home. The Patriots will have to rely on depth players and adjust their game plan as they travel to Hard Rock Stadium, a situation that could reshape the balance of power in the AFC East early in the season.

Brown’s absence is a significant blow to a Patriots offense that has been trying to reestablish a vertical passing attack under head coach Bill O’Brien. The 24‑year‑old rookie, drafted in the first round, has already shown flashes of elite playmaking, posting 350 receiving yards and two touchdowns in the first three games. His route‑running precision and ability to create separation have given quarterback Mac Jones a reliable deep‑ball option, stretching defenses and opening up underneath routes for other playmakers. Without Brown, the Patriots will likely lean more heavily on veteran receiver DeVante Parker and the emerging talent of Jalin Hyatt, who will be tasked with filling the void between the short‑and‑intermediate patterns and the deep threat that Brown provided.

The loss of Henderson, the team’s No. 2 running back, further complicates New England’s offensive outlook. Although he has not yet seen a regular‑season snap, Henderson’s performance in preseason and practice has earned him praise for his burst, vision, and pass‑catching ability out of the backfield. His versatility would have given O’Brien the flexibility to employ a committee approach, mixing power runs with pass‑catching duties to keep the Dolphins’ defense guessing. With Henderson out, the Patriots must turn to backup running backs such as J.J. Taylor and rookie Tyquan Thornton, who have limited NFL experience but have shown promise in limited action. The reduced depth may force the coaching staff to adopt a more pass‑heavy approach, a risky proposition against a Dolphins secondary that has improved markedly since the offseason.

Miami, meanwhile, enters the matchup with a relatively healthy roster and a defense that has been solid against the run but occasionally vulnerable to big plays downfield. The Dolphins’ secondary, anchored by cornerback Xavien Howard and safety Jordan Poyer, has allowed an average of 210 passing yards per game, a statistic that could be attractive for a Patriots unit looking to exploit the absence of its premier receiver. However, Miami’s defensive line, led by Jaelan Phillips, has been effective at pressuring quarterbacks, ranking among the top five in sacks. If the Patriots cannot protect Mac Jones and give him time to work through a reduced receiving corps, the Dolphins could capitalize with a balanced attack that mixes a potent aerial game with a run game that has been gaining consistency under running back Raheem Mostert.

The injury news also has broader implications for the AFC East race. New England, still seeking its first winning season under O’Brien, now faces a must‑win scenario to stay within striking distance of division rivals Buffalo and Miami. The Patriots’ ability to adapt will be a litmus test for the coaching staff’s depth development and game‑planning acumen. For the Dolphins, a victory would not only improve their own standing but also widen the gap between them and a Patriots squad that appears increasingly vulnerable to setbacks.

Looking ahead, the Patriots must quickly reconfigure their offensive scheme, perhaps integrating more screen passes, tight‑end utilization, and creative play‑action to mitigate the loss of Brown and Henderson. The health of both players remains uncertain, and their return could be pivotal for New England’s playoff aspirations later in the season. For now, Sunday’s contest will serve as an early indicator of how resilient the Patriots can be when key pieces are missing, and whether the Dolphins can seize the opportunity to solidify their position atop the division.
